packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-08 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: no proposed identification or reading of this record was revealed in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files in packet-08 (plus crops of them, if noted below). I listed the packet directory once to get image sizes; that listing showed packet.json exists, but I did not open it.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Photograph of an opened paper folder/mount (two panels with central fold) on black ground, colour card lower left, cm scale at right. Two large grey rectangles mask most of both panels (masked by the packet preparer; contents not visible).
- Visible: three small parchment strips taped (with clear tape) onto the lower part of the right panel, below the right mask:
  (a) at left, next to the fold: a small vertical scrap (~2 x 4 cm) with a column of short lines in a black gothic book hand, a red word at top; lines appear to be beginnings of names (one per line), probably a list (e.g. calendar/litany-type list) -- tentative.
  (b) centre: a horizontal strip with red text "festum duplex" (reading from overview), faint other traces.
  (c) right: a small piece with red letters/numerals ("i", "ix"?) -- possibly calendar-type numerals -- tentative.
- Pencil note on the mount lower right: "Stams, StA, Frag. 96 ..."? (modern shelfmark-type note; transcribed only as seen, roughly "Stams, StA, Fzg. 96u"?).
- Images 002-004 are presumably closer views of these strips; checked below.

image-002.jpg -- close view of strip (a), the vertical scrap by the fold
Layout: single narrow column of short lines, each beginning with an enlarged black initial; gothic textualis (formata-like) book hand, black ink; first line in red. Right edge cut through the line-ends; left edge shows the initials (the lower initials damaged/abraded). A faint red stroke left of line 2 in the margin. Scrap is in two pieces (a crease/break between lines 4 and 5) held by clear tape, which causes glare over lines 5-8. Grey mask covers the top right of the image (mount area, not the scrap).
Transcription (lines counted from top of the scrap):
image-002 l.1 (red)  [.]ugusti   -- first letter cut/lost at left; visible "ugusti", final stroke red "-"/flourish?
image-002 l.2  Theodosij ep(iscop)i?   -- "Theodosij" clear; then "ep" with following letter cut at the edge
image-002 l.3  Arnulphi e[...]   -- "Arnulphi" clear; then "e" or "ep" partly cut (looks like "ẽ"/"ep")
image-002 l.4  Arsenij conf(essoris)   -- written "conf." or "cont." with full stop; read conf. (f/t ambiguity)
image-002 l.5  [.]arini e?[...]   -- initial abraded; "arini"? (minims ambiguous: "arun"/"arini"); after it a letter (e/c?) under glare
image-002 l.6  [.]raxed[...]   -- initial abraded (P?); "raxed" then cut
image-002 l.7  [.]arie m[...]   -- initial abraded (M?); "arie" then "m" partly visible
image-002 l.8  Apollinar[...]   -- "Apollinar" (last letters under tape glare/cut)
Limitations: right-hand ends of all lines cut; initials of l.5-7 abraded so first letters not read; tape glare. No numerals/dates visible on this scrap (left margin, if a calendar, is cut away or blank).

image-003.jpg -- close view of strip (b), the horizontal strip; crop made: scratchpad p08-003-right.png (right part, autocontrast, 3x)
Layout: tapering parchment strip; left part blank except one red line; right part shows dry-point/brown vertical ruling (two or three vertical rules forming narrow columns) and horizontal rules, with faded red numerals in a narrow column and large red letters at the right edge -- arrangement resembles a calendar grid (numeral column + letter column) -- tentative interpretation. Black text only as cut-off tops/bottoms of letters at the lower edge.
Transcription (top to bottom; positions are within image-003):
image-003 red line (left, mid-height)  festum duplex.   -- clear, red, with final point
image-003 right, numeral column, upper   [red, faded] iiij? / iiii?   -- minims plus a terminal flourish; could be "iiij" or "xiiij"? uncertain
image-003 right, numeral column, middle  [red, faded] x? / v?   -- a single stroke-pair, possibly "x" or "v" with following point; uncertain
image-003 right, numeral column, lower   [red, faded] iiij? / iii?   -- similar to the upper numeral; uncertain
image-003 right edge, upper   [red large letter] A?   -- triangular capital, likely A (or d); partly cut by the edge
image-003 right edge, lower   [red large letter] B? / g?   -- two-bowled form; B or g, uncertain
image-003 lower edge, black   [...]unifi?[...] / [...]uniu[...]   -- only the tops of a line of black minims, cut off by the edge; not readable with confidence
Limitations: numerals heavily faded; strip edge cuts the black text; the red line "festum duplex" is the only secure reading.

image-004.jpg -- right part of the mount; crop made: scratchpad p08-004-stripc.png (strip c, autocontrast, 3x)
Overlap: the left ~240 px of image-004 repeat the right end of strip (b) already read on image-003 (red large A? and B?/g?, faded numerals, black cut-off letters at bottom edge "...unifi?..."); not counted again.
Strip (c), separate piece to the right, held by tape:
Layout: ruled grid (brown vertical and horizontal rules) like strip (b); a column of red numerals at left, a column of small brown/black letters in the middle, faded red marks at the right (cut edge, notched).
image-004 strip c, left column, top    [red] i    -- a single red minim with hairline, possibly "i" (preceded higher up by a red slanted stroke at the top edge, cut)
image-004 strip c, left column, lower  [red] ix   -- clear "ix" (with a descending tail on the i / x); could be "xix" if a stroke is lost, but read ix
image-004 strip c, middle column, three lines (brown ink, small):
   upper  e? / a?
   middle c? / f?   -- tall letter, partly abraded
   lower  g? / b?
image-004 strip c, right side   [faded red] traces at three line-levels, top one possibly "x?" / "kl?"; illegible
image-004 top edge  a red slanted stroke (cut) above the middle column
Limitations: the brown letters are tiny and abraded, their identity uncertain (they may be letters of a sequence, e.g. calendar letters -- tentative only); right side red text too faded to read.

OVERALL SELECTION / UNREAD AREAS
- Read: all visible text on the three small strips (a), (b), (c) in images 002-004. Large parts of the mount are masked grey in every image (packet preparation); nothing under the masks could be read or surveyed.
- Secure readings: strip (a) list "[.]ugusti" (red) / Theodosij ep... / Arnulphi e... / Arsenij conf. / [.]arini? / [.]raxed... / [.]arie m... / Apollinar...; strip (b) red "festum duplex."; strip (c) red "i", "ix".
- Suggest: reverse sides of the strips if photographed (they are taped down; versos not visible here); raking/UV light for the faded red numerals on (b) and (c).
- Beyond the rules: I made two contrast-enhanced crops (paths above, in the session scratchpad) and listed the packet directory once for image sizes.
